sources.title: Office of the Historian, Syria: recognition and diplomatic relations
sources.note: Direct official history: recognition in 1944, union on 22 February 1958, secession on 28 September 1961. Recognition is distinct from French troop withdrawal.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Syria: A Country Study (1988)
sources.note: Original PDF downloaded and relevant pages extracted. PDF 54, printed 26: evacuation. PDF 23 to 24, printed xix to xx: 1970 and Hama. PDF 84, printed 56: dam. Research completed in 1987; disputed casualty totals are omitted.

sources.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, memorandum of 10 March 1963, document 185
sources.note: Contemporary diplomatic memorandum checked. Use only the coup date and cabinet composition; no Cold War forecasts or value judgments are adopted.

sources.title: Christopher M. Blanchard, Syria: Transition and U.S. Policy, 5 September 2025
sources.note: Original 41-page CRS PDF checked. Printed 1, footnote 1; printed 5 conflict synopsis; printed 6 transitional framework. The report date is 5 September 2025. Its characterization of a 2024 war ending is not treated as proof that all violence ended.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, statement on Syria, 8 December 2024
sources.note: Original UN statement of 8 December 2024 checked: fall of the regime and need for an inclusive transition.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, statement on the Syrian government and SDF agreement, 30 January 2026
sources.note: Original UN statement of 30 January 2026 checked: an agreement and appeal for implementation, not proof of completed implementation.

sources.title: UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, week of 20 to 26 June 2026
sources.note: Indexed original Syria section checked. The 22 June briefing describes participation, justice, delays and insecurity. Direct fetch failed. This is a dated account, not a live situation report.

sources.title: British Museum, Syrian 200-pound banknote, 1997, 2003, 1004.2
sources.note: Original object catalogue checked: cotton loom, woman, workers, factory and cotton plant. Official imagery is not a statistical account of working conditions.

sources.title: UNESCO, Craftsmanship of Aleppo Ghar soap, 2024 nomination 02132
sources.note: Original indexed nomination and 2023 photograph captions checked. Wooden shoes, rake, hand stamp, drying and family transmission. Nomination and captions grouped as one work.

sources.title: UNESCO, Damascene rose practices in Al-Mrah, 2019 nomination 01369
sources.note: Original indexed nomination and 2019 decision checked. Direct pages present a JavaScript challenge. Family harvest, tea, distillation, jam and pastries. No medicinal efficacy claim.

sources.title: UNESCO, decision 13.COM 10.a.7: Syrian shadow play, 2018
sources.note: Original indexed 2018 decision and nomination captions checked. Karakoz, Eiwaz, cafe performance and decline. No claim about current practitioner numbers.

sources.title: Syrian Constitution of 1950, Arabic transcription held by International IDEA
sources.note: Later typeset Arabic transcription, 33 pages, downloaded. Article 28, printed 8 and PDF page 8, first sentence visually checked in constitution-page8.png. Other clauses contain transcription gaps; the chosen line is complete. Romanization and literal English translation are editorial. This is not an original 1950 facsimile or current law.

sources.title: UNICEF, Rebuilding children’s dreams by repairing schools, 21 November 2023
sources.note: Original report dated 21 November 2023 checked. Al Tabni repairs finished in December 2022. Sohaib is twelve; the school has sixteen classrooms plus a preschool classroom. One local case.

sources.title: UNICEF, Bringing schools back to life, 5 November 2025
sources.note: Full original photo essay dated 5 November 2025 checked. Nazih Munzer School, Jaramana: solar power, accessible toilet, ramps, handrails and over 2,300 students in two shifts.

sources.title: WHO, Vaccines on the move, 28 August 2025
sources.note: Original indexed opening of WHO report dated 28 August 2025 checked. Al-Burj camp, Idlib: hospital teams, coolers and loudspeaker. Direct fetch returned 502. No dose count or unverified outcome.

sources.title: Sapienza University, Fifty years after the 1975 Ebla archive discovery
sources.note: Original 2025 university anniversary announcement checked: 1975 discovery; over 17,000 inventory numbers corresponding to about 5,000 tablets. Ancient objects are distinct from the modern discovery.

sources.title: UNESCO, restoration of the Lion of Al-lāt, 5 October 2017
sources.note: Original report dated 5 October 2017 checked. Ancient lion damaged in 2015, fragments moved to Damascus and restored in 2017. Its modern conservation, not ancient manufacture, belongs to this state period.

Imported border coordinates remain unchanged. Historical events and map coverage are distinguished in prose; see batchIdentityNotes for conflicts.

proposedOverrides.summary: The modern Syrian state through independence, union, authoritarian rule, war and transition, with local stories of work, learning and recovery.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact modern Syria only. Index begins in 1945 and is open-ended; five geometry intervals run 1945 to 1960, 1960 to 1994, 1994 to 2000, 2000 to 2010 and 2010 to 2020. Each tested outline contains Damascus, Aleppo, Hasakah and Quneitra, and excludes Beirut and Tripoli in Lebanon. No live-front or legal-border assertion. Keep Assyria, Arameans, Seleucids, Ottomans, Palmyra and Ebla distinct. The 1958 to 1961 union is explained despite the atlas label; December 2024 is a regime change, not an end to a civilization.
